description: Verify that DUT learns from a received (non-gratuitous) ARP Response and uses the cached MAC for the next UDP egress, after announcing via its own ARP Request — Response variant of ARP_39
approach:
[Objective]
Response variant of ARP_39. The seeding stimulus is an ARP Reply addressed to DUT (not a Request); the receive-side merge must populate the cache the same way. Same order requirement: DUT's own announce Request first, then UDP carrying the learned MAC.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Reply injected
   • opcode      = 2
   • sender_ip   = HOST-1-IP, sender_mac = MAC-ADDR1
   • target_ip   = DUT IP
   ⇒ DUT learns <HOST-1-IP, MAC-ADDR1>.

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup → stimulates UDP egress.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   a. DUT's own ARP Request (announce)
   b. DUT → Tester: UDP with eth_dst == MAC-ADDR1

[Pass condition]
Both (a) and (b) observed in order, UDP eth_dst == MAC-ADDR1.

[Fail condition]
Same as ARP_39 — Fail_no_dut_request / Fail_udp_before_dut_request / Fail_wrong_eth_dst / Fail_no_udp.

verdicts.Pass: DUT announced and used learned MAC — Response-side learning works
verdicts.Fail_no_dut_request: DUT did not announce via own Request
verdicts.Fail_udp_before_dut_request: UDP preceded the own Request — order violated
verdicts.Fail_wrong_eth_dst: UDP eth_dst was not the learned MAC
verdicts.Fail_no_udp: DUT did not emit UDP within the window
